dimensions.evidence: Variables table: B and D are counts of persons (unit 1, dimensionless, nonnegative); NI is count of persons (unit 1, signed). Expression B - D is persons minus persons = persons, matching the record's translation_notes. No scaling constants or unit conversions. Consistent with scope (level form; rate form is sibling b02).

guards-inverses.evidence: Guards B >= 0 and D >= 0 match both rejection_cases: negative B (-100) rejected as domain violation, missing D rejected as missing-input. Inverse notes give B = NI + D and D = B - NI, linear with no singularities; substitution check recomputed: 150000 + 750000 = 900000 exactly. Zero case B = D -> NI = 0 verified against balanced-boundary reference (600000 - 600000 = 0). Record explicitly disclaims causal invertibility (count does not identify age-specific fertility/mortality schedules). Algebraic reversibility is not presented as causal invertibility.

reference-independence.evidence: Recomputed all three references by direct subtraction, independent of the record's stated method: ordinary-surplus 900000 - 750000 = 150000 matches expected 150000.0; natural-decrease 500000 - 700000 = -200000 matches expected -200000.0; balanced-boundary 600000 - 600000 = 0 matches expected 0.0. Cases are materially distinct (surplus, signed deficit, zero boundary). Provenance labels are honest: two independent-derivation arithmetic checks plus one limiting-identity; these are definitional arithmetic recomputations, not published external oracles. No oracle misrepresentation.

rights-provenance.evidence: Eurostat ESMS page version pinned and verified on-page: metadata last update 27 July 2026 (sections 2.1-2.3 and footer). Eurostat license claim verified: Commission legal notice states EU-owned website content is licensed CC BY 4.0 with attribution unless otherwise indicated. PRB glossary (2020-10-02 resource page) used only as brief corroborating paraphrase; record qualifies it as copyrighted, cite-briefly. Proposed source use in the record is short paraphrase plus locator only, with explicit no-redistribution statements; my review likewise paraphrases without verbatim reproduction. This passes review of version/terms qualification; it does not grant legal clearance.

scope.evidence: Scope is explicit and bounded: inputs are period flow counts of live births and deaths sharing the same territory and reference period; output is the signed surplus/deficit. Assumptions separate the Eurostat source wording from the curator's application profile (annual, intercensal, projections). Limitations state counts do not standardise for size/age structure (points to b02 rate) and do not separate fertility vs mortality contributions. No overclaim of empirical validity for a definitional identity.

source-fidelity.evidence: r2 repoint verified live: the general ESMS URL (demo_gind_esms.htm, HTTP 200) section 3.4 'Statistical concepts and definitions' contains the entry 'Natural change of population' defining it as the difference between the number of live births and the number of deaths during the year, with positive natural change = natural increase (births outnumber deaths) and negative = natural decrease. This exactly supports the record's original_equation and evidence paraphrase, and cures the r1 defect (Poland national metadata page lacking the definition). Output symbol NI is flagged as introduced, not a source symbol; B/D map to source terms 'live births'/'deaths'. PRB glossary independently corroborates: 'Natural Increase (or Decrease): the surplus (or deficit) of births over deaths in a population in a given time period', plus a Balancing Equation entry consistent with the b01 balance.

models.permitted_use: Compute signed natural-increase counts NI = B - D from nonnegative period flow counts of live births (B) and deaths (D) that share the same territory and reference period, for descriptive demographic accounting (annual, intercensal, or projection intervals). Not permitted: inferring age-specific fertility or mortality schedules from NI; standardised cross-population comparison on counts alone (use the crude rate sibling); or use with mismatched periods/territories.

sources.finding: Section 3.4 Statistical concepts and definitions, entry 'Natural change of population': paraphrased, it is the difference between live births and deaths during the year; positive natural change (natural increase) when births exceed deaths, negative (natural decrease) when deaths exceed births. Page also states population change has two components: natural change and net migration. Metadata last update shown as 27 July 2026.
